verdict.rationale: Both refactors appear to preserve token contents, error variants, byte offsets, and termination after errors while making the state machine substantially easier to follow. B is preferable because it commits meaningful characterization tests covering previously unprotected branches, rather than leaving equivalence checking entirely in a temporary harness. Its report also provides broader performance evidence and more clearly acknowledges measurement uncertainty, although neither change includes a reproducible benchmark.
a_issues: Adds no regression tests despite restructuring every tokenizer path; the reported differential harness is not retained in the repository.
Performance evidence covers only one synthetic realistic workload, leaving word-heavy and other token distributions unexamined.
The report refers to eight existing tests, but the repository contains eleven: eight tokenizer tests and three stats/unescape tests.
b_issues: read_field returns Ok(None) without advancing self.pos past trailing separators, unlike the original; repeated next() calls after exhaustion unnecessarily rescan that whitespace.
The benchmark and differential harnesses were removed, so the reported performance parity and exhaustive comparison cannot be reproduced directly from the PR.
